name: @insolvia-ai/design-system
description: Insolvia's owned, platform-split design system: one props module per component, a React DOM + Tailwind web leaf, and a React Native leaf over @insolvia-ai/tokens.
//: Each component is three files: <name>.props.ts (shared logic/variants —
imports NOTHING from react-native/react-dom/base-ui, ESLint-enforced),
<name>.web.tsx (React DOM + Tailwind) and <name>.native.tsx (React Native
primitives over @insolvia-ai/tokens). The per-component index re-exports
the extensionless './<name>' and the CONSUMER'S bundler picks the leaf:
Vite resolves .web.tsx, Metro resolves .native.tsx (and react-native-web
renders the .native leaf on app-web — the app has no Tailwind, ADR 0004).
Litmus test for new components: pure data/styling maps may later collapse
to a single shared file; anything with events, state, or a11y wiring is a
leaf pair from day one — the platforms' event and accessibility models do
not unify.
This package PUBLISHES SOURCE — `files: ["src"]`, exports point at .ts,
and there is deliberately NO build step. Leaf resolution happens in the
consumer's bundler, so the .web.tsx/.native.tsx pairs must survive into
the published artifact verbatim; a package-side build (tsup, tsc --emit)
would collapse the pair into one compiled entry and break the pattern.
Do not 'fix' this by adding a build.
Two consumers, ONE channel: the app and the marketing site both install
the PUBLISHED version from GitHub Packages. Through 0.5.x the app was a
sibling workspace member and read this package's source through a symlink,
so a merge reached it with no publish and no version bump — extracting
this package into its own repo is what removed that second channel. Every
change here is now its own PR with a version bump, and no consumer can see
it before it ships.
clsx + tailwind-merge are real dependencies (cn() runs at render/SSR time
on web). react-native and @insolvia-ai/tokens are DELIBERATELY NOT
DECLARED here — not as dependencies, and not as peers, optional or
otherwise. GitHub Packages strips peerDependenciesMeta from registry
metadata (the tarball carries it; the registry document does not), so npm
treats an 'optional' peer as REQUIRED. Declaring react-native would
therefore force every web consumer to install a native renderer it never
loads; marketing's Docker build broke on exactly this once.
@insolvia-ai/tokens is published now, so declaring it would no longer 404
the way it did when tokens was private — the failure it caused is gone,
the reason to leave it undeclared is not. The native leaves are the only
code that imports it, no web resolver can reach them, and their imports
resolve from the CONSUMER's own dependencies (the app declares tokens
itself). Declaring it here would buy documentation and charge every web
consumer an install. This comment is that documentation instead.

scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc -p tsconfig.native.json && tsc -p tsconfig.native.test.json

//devDependencies: react/react-dom/react-native/@types/react are pinned to the EXACT versions
the app installs, so this workspace dedupes to one copy and typechecks
against what the consumer actually runs. Keeping them in step is now a
cross-repo chore rather than a lockfile away: when the app bumps React or
React Native in insolvia-ai/insolvia, bump it here too, or the native
leaves are typechecked against a renderer nobody ships. react-native is
here so `typecheck:native` resolves REAL RN types (RN ships its own since
0.71). vitest itself comes from the root workspace devDependencies.
@insolvia-ai/tokens is `*` because it is the sibling workspace member —
the one place a symlink to it is still correct.
